# Final Review Proposal
**Producer:** agent:codex/gpt-5.4

## Summary

I reviewed the changed alkalinity-accounting code and ran focused tank_core tests; the plumbing itself looks internally consistent, but I found two blocking review issues: the patch does not implement the shrimp-scenario deliverable described by the bead, and the only new test file is currently untracked.

## Amendments

1. The patch is functionally unrelated to the requested shrimp-scenario bead. The only added integration tests are nitrification/alkalinity checks at crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:63, :107, :147, :205, :243, and :278, and the code changes in crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:229, crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:12, crates/tank_core/src/systems/water_change.rs:131, and crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:66 are all alkalinity-accounting plumbing. None of the required shrimp scenarios (breeding success, thermal suppression, chemistry stress, chloride protection, crash mode), per-stage shrimp/water dumps, or the required e2e runner/report are present, so this does not satisfy the bead’s acceptance criteria.
   Rationale: This is a blocking correctness gap: the submitted work does not implement the task it is supposed to land.
2. The only new test file, crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:1, is still untracked. `git diff` contains only the src/ changes, so unless this file is explicitly added before submission, the new alkalinity-budget logic will land without any of the accompanying regression coverage.
   Rationale: As submitted, the patch can merge source changes while silently dropping the tests that are supposed to validate them.
